title.narrative: Center for justice and international law, CEJIL, Latin America 2023 - 2027
Centrum för rättvisa och internationell rätt, CEJIL, Latinamerika, 2023 - 2027

description.narrative:
The strategic objective of CEJIL is to:
Strengthen the effectiveness of International Human Rights Law and the mechanisms for protection, as well as the solidity of democratic actors and institutions to guarantee the full exercise of human rights, particularly for historically excluded populations.
CEJIL has identified six specific objectives in their strategic plan:
1. Contribute to reducing inequality and exclusion and guarantee the access of historically discriminated populations to the exercise of rights individually or collectively
2. Guarantee access to justice and the obtaining of transformative reparations for victims of structural violence and serious human rights violations through the use of the Inter-American System for Human Rights.
3. Strengthen the conditions for democracy in the region through judicial independence and freedom of expression
4. Support plural and open societies through the protection of defenders, the generation of alliances and the promotion of civil space at the local and international level.
5. Contribute to the development and strengthening of an international system for the protection of human rights that is effective for the protection and promotion of human rights in the Americas
6. Strengthen the organization's capabilities to guarantee its sustainability, effectiveness and impact.
The expected impact of the work is that:
Historically excluded and at-risk populations in the region, with emphasis on defenders, women, indigenous people, migrants and Afro-descendant populations, are progressively advancing in the exercise of their human rights and have greater access to restorative justice in their countries and internationally.

Det övergripande målet med insatsen är att:
Stärka effektiviteten av internationell rätt avseende mänskliga rättigheter samt skyddsmekanismer, såväl som soliditeten hos demokratiska aktörer och institutioner för att garantera att de mänskliga rättigheterna åtnjuts fullt ut, särskilt för historiskt exkluderade grupper.
För att nå detta arbetar CEJIL i linje med sex specifika mål:
1. Bidra till att minska ojämlikhet, ojämställdhet och utanförskap och garantera tillgången för historiskt diskriminerade grupper till att utöva rättigheter individuellt eller kollektivt.
2. Garantera tillgång till rättvisa och erhållande av transformerande åtgärder för gottgörelse till offer för strukturellt våld och allvarliga kränkningar av de mänskliga rättigheterna genom användning av det interamerikanska systemet för mänskliga rättigheter.
3. Stärka förutsättningarna för demokrati i regionen genom att verka för rättsligt oberoende och yttrandefrihet
4. Stöd till mångfald och öppna samhällen genom skydd av försvarare av mänskliga rättigheter, skapande av allianser och främjande av det demokratiska utrymmet på lokal och internationell nivå.
5. Bidra till utvecklingen och förstärkningen av ett internationellt system för skydd av mänskliga rättigheter som är effektivt avseende skydd och främjande av mänskliga rättigheter i regionen.
6. Stärka organisationens förmåga att garantera hållbarhet, effektivitet och genomslagskraft.

title.narrative: Decision on contribution, CEJIL core support

description.narrative:
CEJIL: Key Achievements in Human Rights Defense in 2025
In 2025 CEJIL maintained 218 active legal matters across the Americas, including 158 cases, 43 precautionary measures, and 15 provisional measures. More than 31, 200 beneficiaries reached through litigation, advocacy, and protection actions. Over 10,000 human rights defenders supported and protected. 4 new strategic cases incorporated and additional cases under review. Historic advances before the Inter-American Human Rights System, including one landmark judgment, multiple hearings, compliance monitoring processes, and new precautionary measures granted. 25 training activities conducted, reaching more than 1,500 participants. 12 publications produced to strengthen knowledge, advocacy, and human rights protection across the region. Strong presence in key countries, with the highest number of active cases in Guatemala (30), Colombia (26), and Brazil (25).
SO1. Contribute to reducing inequality and exclusion and guarantee the access of historically discriminated populations to the exercise of rights individually or collectively.
Most significant achievements in Gender Equality and Women's Rights:
Through strategic litigation and advocacy before regional and international human rights bodies, CEJIL contributed to major advances in gender equality and reproductive rights across Latin America. Key achievements included the creation of the Independent Interdisciplinary Group of Experts (GIEI) in Honduras to advance accountability in the Berta Cáceres case, and a landmark Inter-American Court judgment holding Peru internationally responsible for forced sterilizations. This historic ruling established important regional standards on informed consent, reparations, and reproductive health rights, particularly benefiting Indigenous women and strengthening guarantees of non-repetition.
CEJIL also helped drive structural reforms that improved women's rights and access to justice. In Costa Rica, strategic litigation contributed to the elimination of discriminatory labor practices affecting women workers, resulting in fairer working conditions and stronger labor protections. In El Salvador, sustained advocacy following the Beatriz case reinforced international standards on sexual and reproductive rights and influenced key recommendations from international human rights mechanisms. Additionally, CEJIL supported progress in reparations and recognition for women affected by human rights violations in Colombia and Brazil, advancing accountability and restorative justice.
Most significant achievements in Indigenous Peoples' Rights
CEJIL contributed to strengthening the rights of Indigenous Peoples through strategic litigation, regional advocacy, and partnerships with Indigenous organizations and leaders. In Paraguay, CEJILs work helped advance accountability and implementation of international human rights decisions related to Indigenous land rights and access to essential services, encouraging renewed state commitments and concrete progress for affected communities.
At the regional level, CEJIL strengthened alliances to promote truth, justice, and reparations for Indigenous Peoples, while supporting advocacy before international human rights mechanisms. CEJIL also collaborated with Indigenous women leaders from the Amazon to develop a shared agenda on climate justice, territorial protection, and participation in decision-making, amplifying Indigenous voices and leadership in regional and international discussions.
SO2. Guarantee access to justice and the obtaining of transformative reparations for victims of structural violence and serious human rights violations through the use of the InterAmerican System for Human Rights.
In 2025, CEJIL played a pivotal role in advancing access to justice and transformative reparations for victims of serious human rights violations across the Americas. Through strategic litigation before the Inter-American human rights system, CEJIL helped secure landmark legal decisions in Brazil and Peru that strengthened accountability and challenged impunity, while also supporting concrete reparations measures, including land restitution in Chile and the implementation of a historic, fully funded reparation agreement in Mexico after nearly three decades.
At the international level, CEJIL contributed to strengthening accountability mechanisms for Nicaragua by supporting expanded UN monitoring and mobilizing diplomatic engagement. These efforts increased international pressure on ongoing violations and reinforced victims participation in justice processes. Collectively, CEJILs work helped translate legal recognition of rights into tangible improvements in access to justice, reparations, and protection for affected communities.
In the area of climate justice and human rights, CEJIL was a key actor behind the landmark Inter-American Court Advisory Opinion OC-32/25, which recognizes climate change as a serious and urgent human rights crisis and establishes important regional standards for state action. Through legal advocacy, scientific evidence, coalition-building, and engagement with more than 1,500 stakeholders, CEJIL helped shape this historic outcome and promote its implementation across the region.
CEJIL also advanced regional efforts linking methane emissions, human rights, and climate change by translating complex scientific evidence into legal tools that support communities and judicial processes. Its advocacy contributed to greater recognition of methane as a human rights issue, influenced UN discussions, and supported the inclusion of methane and human rights on the MERCOSUR 2025-2026 agenda. Together, these achievements underscore CEJILs leadership in strengthening human rights protections, accountability, and climate justice in the Americas.
SO3. Strengthen the conditions for democracy in the region through judicial independence and freedom of expression.
Strengthening Democratic Conditions
In 2025, CEJIL played a leading role in defending judicial independence and freedom of expression across the Americas, contributing to stronger democratic safeguards and institutional accountability. Through strategic litigation and international advocacy, CEJIL advanced landmark cases that challenge the criminalization of journalists, promoted judicial reform efforts in Guatemala, and supported constitutional protections in Argentina.
At the regional level, CEJIL strengthened collaboration among judicial actors and human rights defenders to protect the rule of law and respond to democratic backsliding. In Chile, it also helped secure concrete progress in community access to media and information rights. Complementing these efforts, CEJILs public awareness campaigns increased understanding of the importance of independent justice systems. Together, these results reinforced democratic institutions, protected civic space, and expanded access to fundamental rights across the region.
Mitigating Democratic Crises
In 2025, CEJIL played a critical role in defending civic space and protecting human rights defenders in the face of growing democratic backsliding across the region. Through strategic litigation, evidence-based advocacy, and engagement with international human rights mechanisms, CEJIL helped strengthen regional protections against restrictive measures targeting civil society.
In Peru, CEJIL contributed to a landmark Inter-American Court decision that recognized the harmful effects of the APCI Law on civil society organizations, setting an important regional precedent against measures that restrict or criminalize human rights work. In Venezuela, CEJIL documented and exposed the use of passport annulments as a tool of repression, bringing international attention to this practice before the Inter-American and UN human rights systems. Together, these efforts increased accountability, strengthened international protection standards, and enhanced visibility of emerging forms of repression across the Americas.
SO4. Support plural and open societies through the protection of defenders, the generation of alliances and the promotion of civil space at the local and international level.
Protection of Human Rights Defenders and Civic Space
In 2025, CEJIL played a leading role in strengthening the protection of human rights defenders and civic space across Latin America through strategic litigation, policy advocacy, emergency protection measures, and innovative digital and data-driven initiatives. Its work contributed to major advances, including Brazils adoption of a National Protection Plan for Human Rights Defenders, landmark accountability and protection outcomes in Colombia, and international recognition of digital rights protections through a precedent-setting Meta Oversight Board decision.
CEJIL also secured urgent protection measures for defenders at risk, including the release of Venezuelan journalist and defender Carlos Correa, while supporting defenders in El Salvador and Colombia. At the regional level, CEJIL developed innovative tools to improve state monitoring of violence against defenders, helping translate international human rights standards into stronger policies, judicial precedents, and more effective protection systems. Together, these achievements strengthened civic space, enhanced accountability, and improved safeguards for human rights defenders throughout the region.
SO5. Contribute to the development and strengthening of an international system for the protection of human rights that is effective for the protection and promotion of human rights in the Americas.
Strengthening International Human Rights Governance
In 2025, CEJIL played a leading role in advancing more inclusive, transparent, and accountable international human rights institutions. Through its GQUAL campaign and advocacy before the OAS, the United Nations, and the Inter-American System, CEJIL promoted gender equality, transparency in international appointments, and greater civil society participation in decision-making processes.
Key achievements included supporting the implementation of CEDAW General Recommendation No. 40 on equal representation, contributing to reforms and public scrutiny in international selection processes, and helping advance the election of the first woman Assistant Secretary General of the OAS. CEJIL also strengthened public participation in the selection of Inter-American human rights commissioners and helped shape global discussions on leadership in international institutions. Together, these efforts reinforced the legitimacy, representativeness, and effectiveness of international human rights governance in the Americas and beyond.
SO6. Strengthen the organization's capabilities to guarantee its sustainability, effectiveness and impact.
Institutional Strengthening and Sustainability
In 2025, CEJIL strengthened its institutional capacity, sustainability, and regional impact, enhancing its ability to respond effectively to evolving human rights challenges across the Americas. Through strategic communications, organizational improvements, resource mobilization, and capacity-building initiatives, CEJIL expanded its reach and reinforced its role as a leading human rights organization in the region.
CEJIL produced influential research, tools, and advocacy resources on key issues including judicial independence, migration, climate justice, digital security, and gender equality, while delivering training programs that benefited approximately 1,500 human rights defenders, journalists, justice operators, and public officials. At the same time, the organization strengthened its governance, accountability, and operational systems, secured new funding partnerships, and advanced institutional learning through the evaluation of its Strategic Plan. Together, these efforts increased CEJILs resilience, effectiveness, and long-term capacity to drive human rights protection, accountability, and social change across the Americas.
List of Publications in 2025
During 2025, CEJIL published a variety of reports, studies, bulletins, and practical guides addressing key human rights issues in Latin America.
Some of the most notable publications include: Judicial Independence in Central America, an analysis of the weakening of justice systems and the challenges facing the rule of law across the region.
Findings Report on the Visit of Civil Society Organizations to CATEM EMISUR documenting human rights violations against migrants linked to the agreement between Costa Rica and the United States.
Passport Cancellations in Venezuela, highlighting the humanitarian consequences of this practice, including family separation, forced exile, and employment and emotional hardships.
Migration Policies, Borders, and Pathways, a regional bulletin examining migration trends and recent policy developments in Mexico and Central America.
Methane: Health and Human Rights, a publication exploring the impacts of methane emissions on health and their relationship to human rights and the climate crisis.
Expert Evidence Compendium in the Beatriz v. El Salvador Case which brings together expert testimonies presented before the InterAmerican Court of Human Rights in this landmark case.
Two publications from the GQUAL Campaign, focused on advancing women´s equal representation and gender parity in international decision-making spaces.
A Practical Guide for Reporting Threats Against Human Rights Defenders on Facebook, Instagram, and Threads, designed to strengthen protection and response mechanisms against digital violence and online abuse
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
